'''Michael Anthony Viscardi''' (born February 22, 1989, in [[Plano, Texas|Plano]], [[Texas]]) of [[San Diego, California|San Diego]], [[California]], is an American [[mathematician]] who, as a highschooler, won the 2005 [[Siemens Competition]] and [[Davidson Fellow]]ship with a mathematical project on the [[Dirichlet problem]], whose applications include describing the flow of heat across a metal surface, winning $100,000 and $50,000 in scholarships, respectively.<ref>{{Citation |url=https://www.usatoday.com/news/nation/2005-12-05-homeschooledscience_x.htm |title=Problems no problem for Siemens winners |newspaper=[[USA Today]] |date=December 5, 2005 |first=Tracey Wong |last=Briggs }}.</ref><ref>{{Citation |url=http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/education/2002667009_sciencekid06.html |title=California teen wins science competition |newspaper=[[Seattle Times]] |date=December 6, 2005 |first=Juan-Carlos |last=Rodriguez }}.</ref> Viscardi's theorem is an expansion of the 19th-century work of [[Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet]].<ref>{{Citation |url=https://abcnews.go.com/WNT/TenWays/story?id=2128438 |title=Teen Updates 19th-Century Mathematical Law |work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |date=December 9, 2005 }}.</ref> He was also named a finalist with the same project in the [[Intel Science Talent Search]]. Viscardi placed Best of Category in Mathematics at the International Science and Engineering Fair ([[ISEF]]) in May 2006. Viscardi also qualified for the [[United States of America Mathematical Olympiad]] and the Junior Science and Humanities Symposium.

==Life==
Viscardi was [[Homeschooling|homeschooled]] for high school, supplemented with mathematics classes at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref>{{Citation |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna10336018 |title=Homeschooled teen wins top science honor |newspaper=Associated Press |date=2005}}</ref><ref name=FOCUS>{{Citation |title=Mathematics Student Wins the Siemens-Westinghouse Competition |periodical=FOCUS |publisher=Mathematical Association of America |volume=26 |issue=1 |page=3 |date=January 2006}}</ref> He is also a pianist and violinist, and onetime concertmaster
of the San Diego Youth Symphony.<ref name=FOCUS/>

Viscardi is a member of the [[Harvard College]] class of 2010.<ref>[http://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2008/06/herchel-smith-research-fellows/ Herchel Smith Research Fellows to begin this summer]</ref> He graduated summa cum laude from Harvard, receiving a 2010 [[Thomas T. Hoopes, Class of 1919, Prize]], and earning the 2011 [[Morgan Prize]] honorable mention for his senior thesis "Alternate Compactifications of the Moduli Space of Genus One Maps".<ref>{{Cite arXiv|eprint = 1005.1431|last1 = Viscardi|first1 = Michael|title = Alternate compactifications of the moduli space of genus one maps|year = 2010|class = math.AG}}</ref> He worked as a postdoc at [[UC Berkeley]] from 2016 to 2018.<ref>[https://math.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/michael-viscardi Viscardi's webpage at Berkeley]</ref>
